$comment: CONFIGURE TIME ONLY — never read at run time, and not installed (cmake/DssInstall.cmake excludes this directory). `quotedSourceTextLimit` is the most bytes of source text ONE diagnostic quotes. Every diagnostic that names an operand, a declarator, an attribute clause or a token by its spelling quotes it through one rendering, `quotedSourceText` (core/types/diagnostic_quote.hpp): the text is put on one line (a run of white space that holds a line break becomes one space), and past this many bytes it is cut at a character boundary and ends in an ellipsis (U+2026, a character no C source spells). The snippet under the header carries the location; the quote only names what is there. WHY A LIMIT: a quote used to be the operand's whole text, so one diagnostic grew with the expression it named, and a nest of N conditionals printed O(N²) bytes — ✔MEASURED, conditionals nested 8 / 32 / 128 deep one level per line, stderr bytes: DSS 4181 / 20047 / 36259 (the level-31 warning of the 32-deep nest quoted 61 lines), where both working references stay LINEAR (gcc 13.3.0 1003 / 3739 / 14811 prints only the caret's line; clang 18.1.3 3133 / 16390 / 69895 highlights at most 16 snippet lines and names the two TYPES) — [[D-DIAG-A-DIAGNOSTIC-QUOTES-ITS-OPERAND-WHOLE]]. WHY HERE AND NOT IN A RUN-TIME DOCUMENT: the limit is the diagnostics' own, the same for every language, target and object format and for every tier that quotes (the tokenizer, the tree builder, the semantic analyzer, the assembler's lowering), and no run-time document is the diagnostics' — a language document would make every language restate a rendering of ITS diagnostics that is not a fact of the language. CMake reads it when the build is configured (cmake/DssConfigureTimeCount.cmake refuses by name a missing document, one that is not a JSON object, or a value that is not a positive whole number) and compiles it in (src/core/CMakeLists.txt); core/types/diagnostic_quote.cpp refuses to build without that forward, so no default in code stands in for it. THE VALUE: 48 bytes, the bound the analyzer's one bounded rendering already applied (the static-assertion operand suffix, whose cap existed because a span crossing macro expansions once pasted the whole `<built-in>` prologue into one message), so the only change a short quote sees is none — every quote of 48 bytes or fewer is the source text itself, byte for byte.
